known_facts_book1: A huge toy bear of a lovely lavender color who rules the City of Bear Center, walking on his hind legs and wearing a tin crown set with diamonds and amethysts.
Is light lavender rather than royal purple, which the Brown Bear explains is second cousin to purple and therefore good enough for a King.
Is stuffed with extra-quality curled hair, not cotton, and squeaks in the chest whenever anything pushes against it — which in Bear Center it is bad manners to notice.
Carries a short wand of a glittering metal that resembles silver but is not, and with three waves of it conjures the image of Cayke's dishpan and later the image of Ugu himself.
His magic is limited to what the fairies slyly dropped into his stuffing when he was made; he can do that magic and nothing else.
Condemns Cayke and the Frogman to death as a matter of form, the execution to take place ten years hence, since in Oz no one ever dies and in ten years they will all have forgotten.
Rules in his own absence, saying a King is not required to stay at home forever, and threatens naughty bears with being sent to some girl or boy in America to play with.
Carries the little Pink Bear in his arms the whole journey rather than let it out of his sight.
Sulks and refuses to let the Pink Bear be questioned after his oracle is doubted, and is vindicated with 'He never makes a mistake!'
Accepts Ozma's invitation to visit the Emerald City, leaving Corporal Waddle in charge of his bears.

known_relations_book1.the little Pink Bear: His oracle, the best bit of magic he possesses and unique in the world.
known_relations_book1.Corporal Waddle: His sentry, who captures the intruders and is left in charge.
known_relations_book1.Cayke: The Cookie Cook he condemns to death as a formality and then helps.
known_relations_book1.the Frogman: The one member of the party whose honesty he likes from the start.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: Who thanks him and hangs an emerald chain on his Pink Bear.

known_facts_book1: A tiny pink toy bear, smaller than any other in Bear Center, lifeless until the crank in its side is turned.
Can tell anything that HAS happened, anywhere, and his words are always words of truth — but he can tell nothing that is GOING to happen.
Names Ugu the Shoemaker as the thief of Cayke's dishpan, and gives the distance to his castle as nineteen miles and three furlongs northeast of Bear Center.
Answers in rhyme when asked whether the two parties are safe together: 'Safe for you and safe for me; Perhaps no others safe will be.'
Says Ozma is 'in a hole in the ground a half mile away at your left', and is disbelieved when only Button-Bright is found there.
Then says Ozma is NOT in the hole and is 'here, among you', which the party takes for a contradiction and for madness.
Is proved right on every count: Ozma was in the hole because Button-Bright was in it with the peach pit in his pocket, and was among them for the same reason.
Finally names the exact place: in Button-Bright's left-hand jacket pocket.
Receives a chain of emeralds from Ozma's own neck, and thanks her — after the King turns his crank.

known_relations_book1.the Lavender Bear: His King, who carries him and defends his infallibility.
known_relations_book1.Button-Bright: The boy whose pocket held the answer to every one of his replies.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: Whom his answers locate and who honors him for it.

known_facts_book1: A chubby, fuzzy brown toy bear whose head comes about as high as Cayke's waist, stuffed with a very good quality of curled hair and skinned in the best plush ever made.
Is the sentry guarding the way to Bear Center, and carries a gun with a tin barrel, a cork in the end and a string tying the cork to the handle.
Declares the Frogman and Cayke his prisoners, admitting he does not wish to but that it is his duty — and that their trial and execution should afford much entertainment.
Fires the popgun to summon the bears out of every hollow tree in the clearing.
Adds a second charge against the prisoners for having asked whether the bears stole the dishpan.
Protests when the King lets them go unpunished, and pops his cork as a parting salute when the party leaves.
Is left in charge of the bears while the King is away.

known_relations_book1.the Lavender Bear: His King, who overrules his charges and leaves him in command.
known_relations_book1.Cayke: The prisoner who laughs aloud at his threats.
known_relations_book1.the Frogman: The prisoner who agrees to come peaceably.
